summary: In this fiction excerpt from a book's third part, the narrator Morgan receives a phone call from Alan announcing that their trip must leave today despite the storm. Morgan suspects a setup, reasoning that someone wants him out of town and that the change confirms he is on Sarah's trail. Alan's explanations seem evasive, and Morgan pushes him for the real reason. Alan refuses to let Morgan make a phone call to Steve or settle the hotel bill, and insists he be out front in nineteen minutes.
one_line: Morgan, suspecting a setup, is pressed by Alan to leave town immediately in a storm while pursuing the trail of Sarah.
key_facts: Morgan is drying her hair in a large beige towel when the phone rings again.
Alan says there has been a small change of plans and that they must go up today, storm or no.
Morgan believes she is being set up because the weather still looks threatening through the curtain.
Morgan concludes that the sudden trip confirms she is on the trail of Sarah.
Morgan plans to call New York and check out the local Ninos del Mundo that Barry Morton wanted her to see.
Alan claims something heavy has come up for tomorrow, so it must be now or forget it for at least a week.
Morgan says Alan had declared there was no way they would go today.
Alan says he wants to check the address of the Ninos del Mundo in town and possibly cruise by if there is time.
Morgan asks Alan for the real story, and he replies that everything has changed.
Morgan wants Steve to know where she is and plans to tell the desk she is not skipping the bill.
Alan refuses the phone call and tells Morgan to be out front in exactly nineteen minutes.
Alan tells Morgan that this is not a dry run.
